label: ACCEPT
reason: No no-explicit-any rule exists in .eslintrc.js and strict tsc allows explicit any, so not TRIVIAL. Members such as hooks.ts and get-computed.ts are fully typed. The one outlier, get-class-properties-plugin.ts:148-159, uses (item.scope as any).forName and an ad-hoc (child as any)._traversed, even though checkIsForNode/ForNode in types/mitosis-node.ts give a typed scope. That is a choice worth a look, so ACCEPT. I hesitated with WRONG because unexported babel-node helpers in signals/plugins/get-code-processor-plugins.ts also take `node: any`.

label: ACCEPT
reason: Every rule module, such as css-no-vars.ts, ref-no-current.ts and static-control-flow.ts, has a matching RuleTester test in __tests__. The only outlier is index.ts, the one registry that composes the rules, so it is a one_off. A new ESLint rule without tests fails no tool and is clearly worth flagging.

label: WRONG
reason: There is no no-explicit-any lint rule, so this is not TRIVIAL. Most outliers are generic low-level utilities that deal with untyped data by design: the Babel visitor-state generic defaults in babel-transform.ts, a lodash-style set(obj: any) in set.ts, the unknown-narrowing type guard in is-mitosis-node.ts, and objectHasKey over an unconstrained T in typescript.ts. Only the `as any` cast in collect-styled-components.ts:58, plus perhaps dedent's any[], is drift, which makes 2 of 7. I hesitated with ACCEPT, since several of these could use unknown instead.
